comments.text: I think the reason people try to 'deflate' the concept of generative AI is because so many people see it as a magical god, and believe that if we just make it bigger, it will be sentient. Having a wrong understanding causes problems and disappointment. For instance, a single neuron can do more calculation on it's own than we thought, so comparing parameters to neurons doesn't work as well as we thought. Getting a more clear understanding of what it is, and isn't will help people apply it usefully, but will also help us figure out the best way to move forward. To reach AGI we need far more than just more parameters. It may only be six or seven conceptual advances but what we have now, structurally is like ... a calculator compared to a PC. you can make the calculator as big as you want but it'll only ever do math, without the other components working in sync to create a full computer.

comments.author: @Inconito___
comments.text: Firstly human neurons ARE NOT like ANN, the brain doesn't do back propagation to compute the optimal weights of synapses. Neural networks are universal function approximators and have been studied extensively mathwise. We have very strong theoretical insights since BEFORE the 2000s. Firstly, the number of neurons is not everything, depth is fundamental (Telgarsky theorem 2016). And if we take Barron's theorem regarding the evolution of error there are two terms : O(C^2/q) + O(qn*log(N)/N) where q is the number of neurons, n the input dim and N the number of training points (C is a smoothness constant). We clearly see that yes when q is high, yes, the first part is low but the O(qn*Log(N)/N) is also very high (overfitting error) and we therefore need a very big N to balance that out. When you train your model on nearly the whole internet's text, there is not much data left to train the model and get better results (on the other hand humans learn with a continuous multimodal flow of data since their birth)

There are two factors that point towards AI needing less parameters than a human brain to reach the "same level" of intelligence:

First: the human brain allocates a lot of those parameters to biological needs that an AI would not need to. For example we need brain infrastructure to manage an entire body, with everything that's going on with it. The brain literally takes care of everything that happens on your body and that requires an organ to do something.

Second: the quality of the data matters. If the input database has tons of low quality or low significance information, parameters would still be used to process that information and how it connects to the rest. These parameters might as well not be there. Therefore you could do the same with less.
This is evidenciated in the model training technique of using curated data or quality synthetic data to obtain good performance in smaller models.

comments.text:
So GPT 3 has about 175 B parameters. GPT 3.5 has about 375 B parameters, and GPT 4 has about 1.5 T parameters. There apparently haven't been huge changes to the architecture of since GPT 3, just larger and larger data sets / parameters.  Clearly, the increase in parameters / data set size is having a dramatic effect on usefulness / apparent intelligence.  We saw a nearly 10x increase in parameters of Chat GPT in just under 3 years.
